answer: Temporal lineage chaining. Each identity must publish a signed signal at randomized intervals; the next identity must reference the prior one's chain hash. Duplicates fork the chain, and any node can verify divergence. An attacker maintaining N copies pays N concurrent timing slots plus storage for parallel chains, and a single missed interval collapses every dependent identity. Like a vine grafted to one root, the opal marker embedded in each hash makes copied ancestry visibly branch.
